title: Spring News Roundup: First Release Candidates of Boot, Framework, Data, Security, Modulith, AI
gist: During the week of October 19, 2026, the Spring ecosystem shipped coordinated first release candidates across 17 projects, including Spring Boot 4.2.0, Spring Framework 7.1.0, Spring Security 7.2.0 and Spring AI 2.1.0. Notable changes include Spring Cloud Bus being folded into Spring Cloud Stream, Spring AI replacing ChatMemory with a new SessionService, and Spring Modulith adding ABANDONED/RESUBMITTED event states.

insights.claim: In the week of October 19, 2026, Spring shipped first release candidates across 17 projects at once, including Boot, Framework, Data, Cloud, Security, Modulith, AI, Batch and Spring for Apache Kafka.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: GA releases across the whole ecosystem look close, so teams should plan upgrade testing now.
insights.locator: There was a flurry of activity

insights.claim: Spring Boot 4.2.0-RC1 moves to the Ubuntu Resolute builder, replacing the Noble Java Tiny Builder. It also speeds up Uber-Jar performance by looking up classes and resources in nested jars directly.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Container image builds and fat-jar startup behavior change in 4.2.
insights.quote: improved Uber-Jar performance using direct lookup of classes and resources in nested jars
insights.locator: The first release candidate of Spring Boot

insights.claim: Spring Framework 7.1.0-RC1 adds RetryListener overloads, onRetrySuccess() and onRetryFailure(), that pass RetryState so listeners can read the retry state directly. It also improves nullability and removes deprecated APIs.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Removing deprecated APIs means upgrades may need code changes.
insights.locator: The first release candidate of Spring Framework

insights.claim: In Spring Cloud 2026.0.0-RC1 (codename Paddington), based on Spring Boot 4.2.0-RC1, Spring Cloud Bus is no longer a separate project and has been merged into Spring Cloud Stream.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Users of Spring Cloud Bus will need to move their dependencies to Spring Cloud Stream.
insights.quote: Spring Cloud Bus is no longer its own project and has been incorporated into Spring Cloud Stream
insights.locator: The first release candidate of Spring Cloud

insights.claim: Spring AI 2.1.0-RC1 adds a SessionService interface for creating and finding sessions, replacing the now-deprecated ChatMemory interface. OpenAiChatModel and DeepSeekChatModel can now build each choice's assistant message from ordered message parts.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Java LLM apps that use ChatMemory face a migration to session-based conversation state.
insights.quote: a new SessionService interface for creating and finding sessions that replaces the now-deprecated ChatMemory interface
insights.locator: The first release candidate of Spring AI

insights.claim: Spring Modulith 2.2.0-RC1 adds ABANDONED and RESUBMITTED event-publication statuses to tell failed publications apart from abandoned ones. By default it now completes publications within the listener's transaction, via TransactionSynchronization, so a listener cannot commit while the completion fails.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Event-driven modular monoliths become more reliable about consistency.
insights.locator: The first release candidate of Spring Modulith

insights.claim: In Spring Security 7.2.0-RC1, StrictServerWebExchangeFirewall no longer treats a non-canonical-case HTTP method as a distinct value, because HttpMethod.valueOf() now normalizes casing. The opaque token introspectors now set Content-Type to application/x-www-form-urlencoded.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Firewall and token-introspection behavior changes slightly, which may affect edge-case tests.
insights.locator: The first release candidate of Spring Security

insights.claim: Spring Integration 7.2.0-RC1 deprecates the default constructor of SerializingHttpMessageConverter in favor of one that takes an allowedPatterns attribute, for improved security.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Teams should allowlist deserialization patterns explicitly before the default constructor goes away.
insights.quote: a deprecation of the default constructor in the SerializingHttpMessageConverter class to define a new constructor that contains the allowedPatterns attribute for improved security
insights.locator: The first release candidate of Spring Integration
